title: Injectivity of étale restriction from universal Zariski restriction
statement: Let $i:Z\to X$ be a closed immersion of schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Suppose that for every Zariski sheaf of sets $G$ [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image], the canonical unit on global sections $\Gamma(X,G)\to\Gamma(Z,i^{-1}_{\rm Zar}G)$ is bijective. For every sheaf of sets $F$ on the small étale site of $X$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets], the unit restriction $\Gamma(X,F)\to\Gamma(Z,i^{-1}_{\rm et}F)$ is injective. Here restriction is the inverse-image adjunction unit evaluated at the terminal étale object [lem-weil-pbc-sets-finite-surjective-descent]; no quasi-compactness or finite-base-change hypothesis is assumed.

source.place: Tag 09ZF, lemma-gabber-h0, first two proof paragraphs (the injectivity argument)

proof.text: Obtain a continuous inclusion k of the Zariski site into the small étale site, with k followed by the fully faithful forgetful functor equal to X.restrictFunctor. The canonical lift j has the same composite. Lift their equality to a natural isomorphism k ≅ j using fully faithful whiskering; continuity transports along it. Precomposition by j thus gives the canonical Zariski restriction sheaves of F and its inverse image. The pullback square of the restriction to an open yields each required base-change isomorphism and its projection equation.

Apply the Zariski-to-étale comparison theorem to these canonical restriction sheaves and identifications. Its unit equation says that restriction at the top open factors as the Zariski unit followed by the comparison, which is injective. The Zariski unit is bijective by hypothesis, hence this composite is injective.

The top-open inclusion is isomorphic to the identity étale object using Scheme.topIso. Pull sections at the identity back along this isomorphism. Naturality of the inverse-image unit transports an assumed equality of their restrictions to an equality at the top-open inclusion. The comparison-unit equation and comparison injectivity give equality of their Zariski-unit images. Zariski injectivity from the hypothesis gives equality of the sections at the top open. Applying the inverse isomorphism gives equality of the original sections.
